title: Feedback wanted on game visuals
author: KingofKingsofKingsof
selftext:
I personally like the visuals, but worry it is too busy. I'm considering reducing the saturation of the background elements to make the cards pop a bit more.   But I'd like some feedback on whether this looks broadly OK or like puke?

  
Thanks!

  
\- threejs

\- Claude opus 5.5, fully vibe coded

\- ChatGPT sol 6.1 for visuals.  Card template and artwork done separately and then manually put together in MS Paint of all place.

\- Started last night.

comments.author: ufimizm
comments.body: It is too busy, you should definitely backgroundize the background. Tried to concentrate on the cards but my eyes kept coming back to the cityscape in the back.

replies.author: KingofKingsofKingsof
replies.body:
https://i.redd.it/74pa61mjd01i1.png

Thanks.  I've played around with the saturation of each of the elements.

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body: Yeah just off the bat the background should be different from the cards. Right now it all blends together. Ask claude to use chatgpt and come up with better background concepts for a card game that contrast better with the cards.

replies.author: KingofKingsofKingsof
replies.body:
Thanks.  I've played around with the saturation of each of the elements. 

https://i.redd.it/l5nfl5opd01i1.png

comments.author: Lord_Forwind
comments.body:
I'd say make the playing space more of a solid color or not the background? It's hard to describe but the cards don't show up enough on the background. I'd probably get a headache looking at it for ages. 

Maybe try toggles for the playing space art so people can pick what they want.

comments.author: Frosty-Breath-81
comments.body: Yes it's too busy. It's all one layer and its got the gpt-image grid problem. there's things absolutely everywhere and like no solid colors. instantly flags as lazy AI art

replies.author: KingofKingsofKingsof
replies.body:
Sorry what's the gpt grid problem? 

To be clear, gpt didn't design the layout of the playfield. It was my decision to have backgrounds representing different dungeons, to place the cards as they are, and then my decision to frame everything as paintings and to use the medieval wallpaper. Also my decision to go with this art style as I liked it, and to keep the art consistent between cards and backgrounds. So please blame me and my poor taste rather than assuming everything that is crap is due to AI. I've since desaturated the background elements (more so than in the images below), and this seems to separate the cards much more nicely. I'll likely just include options to alter the playfield design so
 people can do what they want.

replies.author: Frosty-Breath-81
replies.body: the grid problem is gpt placing too many details at every spot, resulting in a grid-like layout. you can see it in too many cobblestones, too many bricks, too many roof tiles, too many ripples in the water, too many leaves etc etc. it's like if every dot on pointillism was made to be a different object rather than making up a larger thing.

replies.author: KingofKingsofKingsof
replies.body: Ah, I see, yes. I think I'll see what Gimp can do. A bit of blur, noise reduction, or paint effect might help. I want them to look like paintings, which they don't quite do yet!  Thanks for the explanation

replies.author: Frosty-Breath-81
replies.body: I think you should generate something simple, then do a painting filter over it in an image editor.
